_comment: POST-CUTOVER VALUES (updated 2026-09-08). The site went live on 2026-09-07: publicHostnames/adminHostnames now name the real domains and both base URLs point at them, so this file finally describes what production actually is. Until this update it still held the Phase 10c values — empty hostname arrays and *.azurewebsites.net base URLs — which meant a 'drift re-apply' would have SILENTLY REVERTED THE CUTOVER, snapping every email link back to the Azure hostnames. (1) SECRETS ARE NEVER STORED HERE. postgresAdminPassword, smtpUsername, smtpPassword, seedAdminPassword and seedAdminEmail must be passed on the az CLI at deploy time. Omitting any of them RESETS the Postgres admin password and OVERWRITES the Key Vault SMTP secrets — on a live database serving real guests, so pass the values already in use (Key Vault jmk-ag-prod-kv) rather than new ones, unless you are deliberately rotating. (2) BICEP IS NOT IN CI/CD. The deploy pipelines run AzureWebApp@1 only — application code, no infrastructure — so every Bicep apply is a manual 'az deployment group create'. Do not assume a pipeline reconciles this. (3) The hostname bindings and managed certificates were created imperatively at the cutover (az webapp config hostname add, then ssl.bicep). With the arrays below populated, main.bicep now declares the same end state, so a re-apply should be a genuine no-op for them — that is the whole point of this update. (4) geoRedundantBackup is intentionally not set (defaults off) — see the SKU-limitations section in README.md. (5) POST-REVIEW 2026-09-08: seedAdminPassword is now deliberately EMPTY. AdminSeeder only creates an account when the user table is empty, which production's is not, so supplying it would do nothing except put a live admin password back into readable App Service configuration (finding #3). Supply it only when recovering production into an empty database. Secrets still passed on the CLI are postgresAdminPassword, smtpUsername and smtpPassword — three, not five.
